note_on_method: Two kinds of claim appear below and they are kept apart deliberately. Claims about the world - how many courts a park has, whether they are striped on tennis courts or built for pickleball - come from the City of Spokane's Recreational Fields and Sports page and are cited. Claims about our own coverage are facts about this dataset rather than about Spokane County, and are worded so a reader cannot mistake one for the other. Spokane County is the third Washington county published here and the first east of the Cascades, and one city of it is on this page. That city's page had to be read in a browser, because my.spokanecity.org answers every scripted request with a redirect into a "Checking Your Browser" interstitial, and its re-check is a browser read compared against the saved text.

slots.coverage: One city in Spokane County is published here: Spokane, with six venues and thirty-six courts verified against one City page. Our unverified import places forty-two rows in the county, and the twenty-eight of them in Spokane are the only ones that have been checked against a named source. The rest - five in Spokane Valley, four in Liberty Lake, two in Cheney, one each in Colbert and Millwood, and one whose city field is a road name - have not, and nothing run by the County itself has been read either, so none of them appears anywhere. What this page reports is six parks whose court counts and addresses the City of Spokane publishes and we have read: four where the pickleball courts are stripes on tennis courts, two where the City's own heading is "Dedicated Pickleball Courts". One park inside Spokane itself is absent and named on the city page rather than quietly dropped. Sky Prairie Park appears on the City's striped list as "Sky Prairie Park, 8501 N. Nettleton Ct., 2 Courts", and that address resolves at no house number in the Census geocoder or OpenStreetMap; a venue whose address does not resolve does not publish, and the run is built to fail the day this one does. Spokane County is the third county in Washington on this page's parent state page, after King and Clark, and the first east of the Cascades. Every one of its six published addresses was matched at house-number level and placed in the county and in the incorporated place Spokane.
slots.distribution: What is verified in this county is concentrated in one city and, within it, in two parks. Mission Park holds sixteen courts and Comstock Park twelve - twenty-eight of the county's thirty-six - and each of the other four parks holds two. The two large sets are both stripe counts: the City's tennis list gives Mission eight tennis courts and Comstock six, and its striped list gives each park exactly twice that, so what you find on the day depends on how many tennis matches are under way. Peaceful Valley's two are on one tennis court and A.M. Cannon's two are on two, one to one. Only Corbin Park and Underhill Park, two courts each, are pickleball whenever you arrive. The six parks sit in six named neighbourhoods across the city - Logan, the South Hill, West Central, Peaceful Valley below the bluff west of downtown, Emerson-Garfield north of downtown and East Central - and across four postcodes: 99201 twice, 99202 twice, 99203 and 99205. The split that matters most anywhere else, indoor against outdoor, cannot be drawn here at all, because the City never writes either word against any court; thirty-six courts carry no answer on that line. Lighting is the same: no venue is stated lit and none is stated unlit, so all six read as not verified. Hours are stated nowhere. No court in the county carries a price, because the City's one sentence on access - first-come-first-served, with a reservation permit by online form - names no fee for the permit and never says the courts are free.
slots.gaps: The honest position is that this is a Spokane page wearing the heading of a whole county, and the gap will not close by accident. Spokane Valley and Liberty Lake are the obvious next places, on the rows our import holds for them, and neither has been read. Neither have Cheney, Colbert, Millwood, nor anything the County runs itself. The threshold has not moved - three venues with a named source and a date - and a parks department's page has to be loaded first, which in Spokane's case meant loading it by hand. The gaps inside the published city are gaps in what the City writes down rather than in what it has built, and they are specific. Hours: none, for any park. Lighting: none. Surface: none. Nets: not mentioned. Indoor or outdoor: neither word appears. Price: one sentence for the whole section that names a permit and no fee. Parking: nothing. Each of those is a fact the City could add to the list it already keeps, and the day it does, the build fails and the page is re-read. Two parks on that list are close to publishing and are not. Sky Prairie Park has a count and an address the City writes as "8501 N. Nettleton Ct.", which no resolver finds; the fix is the City's to make or the resolvers' to catch up on. Grant Park, which the imported dataset carried as a pickleball venue, is on the City's tennis list only, with two tennis courts, and on neither pickleball list. Nothing outside a municipal parks department appears here, because no other operator in the county publishes a source we have read.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts are there in Spokane County?
faqs.a: We do not know, and no honest page can tell you. What we have checked is 36 courts across six parks, all in the City of Spokane, each with a source and a date you can see: 32 striped on tennis courts and four dedicated. The City itself lists one more park, Sky Prairie, with two courts at an address that does not resolve.

Because it is the only municipality in the county whose courts we have confirmed against a named source. A city appears here once three or more of its venues carry a source_url and a date_checked. Our import holds rows for Spokane Valley, Liberty Lake, Cheney, Colbert and Millwood, and not one of them has been read.

faqs.q: How was Spokane checked, if its website blocks scripts?
faqs.a: By reading it in a browser. my.spokanecity.org answers every scripted request this project makes with a redirect into a "Checking Your Browser" interstitial, so the City's Recreational Fields and Sports page was opened in a browser on 7 September 2026, its "Tennis and Pickleball Courts" section expanded, and the text saved with a header stating the method. Every line of its three lists is asserted against that file on every build.

faqs.q: Are there indoor or lit courts in the county?
faqs.a: Not stated, at any venue. The City never writes "indoor" or "outdoor" against any court, and states no lighting and no hours for any park, so all six venues read as not verified on both. That is a gap in the record rather than a claim that the courts are outdoors, dark or closed. There is no indoor page and no lights page here for that reason.

faqs.q: Are the courts on this page free?
faqs.a: Not stated, at any venue. The City writes one sentence for every court: they are first-come-first-served, and a court can be officially reserved with a reservation permit by online form. It publishes no price for the permit and never says the courts are free. This site does not assume a park court is free, so cost reads as unstated at all six.

faqs.q: Why is Sky Prairie Park not listed?
faqs.a: The City lists it with two pickleball courts at "8501 N. Nettleton Ct.", and that address resolves at no house number in the Census geocoder or OpenStreetMap. A venue publishes here with an address that resolves as written, and no address is ever taken from outside the operator. The build is written to fail the day the address resolves, so the park cannot stay refused once it is publishable.
